A new asset must not be keyed to the synonym route.
rejectedAssets.requiredResolution: Retire the synonym slug in favor of an Eubacteriales canonical record keyed to NCBITaxon:186802, while preserving Clostridiales in source-specific historical taxon labels.

rejectedAssets.reason: NCBI Taxonomy assigns NCBITaxon:1496 to the current name Clostridioides difficile and records Clostridium difficile as its homotypic synonym. LPSN lists Clostridioides difficile as the correct name explicitly recommended for medical use, while the 2016 Lawson et al. paper supplies the primary new combination. A second canonical route or asset would duplicate the same organism.
rejectedAssets.requiredResolution: Merge the duplicate source associations and nomenclatural context into the Clostridioides difficile canonical record, retire the historical-combination slug, and preserve source-era uses of Clostridium difficile without creating a second taxon.
rejectedAssets.routingImpact: The obsolete slug is excluded from the canonical queue, registry, public media files, and image sitemap. No raster exists for either duplicate; a future asset may be keyed only to clostridioides-difficile and NCBITaxon:1496.
rejectedAssets.resolution: The duplicate historical-combination record was merged without dropping its six source associations or name-change provenance. Its article, history, and suggest routes permanently redirect to the single current Clostridioides difficile record.

rejectedAssets.reason: The ICTF Working Group on Dothideomycetes recommends Cladosporium Link 1816 over the younger sexual-morph name Davidiella Crous & U. Braun 2003 under one-fungus/one-name treatment. Species Fungorum accepts Cladosporium, and NCBI Taxonomy assigns genus TaxID 5498 to Cladosporium. A second canonical route or asset would duplicate the selected genus.
rejectedAssets.requiredResolution: Merge the supported historical Davidiella observation and source-label context into the Cladosporium record, retire the obsolete genus slug, and preserve source-era uses of Davidiella without creating a second canonical taxon or media asset.
rejectedAssets.routingImpact: The obsolete slug is excluded from the canonical queue, registry, public media files, and image sitemap. The existing reviewed Cladosporium asset remains the sole current-route asset keyed to NCBITaxon:5498.
rejectedAssets.resolution: The Davidiella route was retired after the only supported historical observation was merged into Cladosporium with its original label and limitations. Six unrelated declared source associations and uncited metal, colonization, and disease mechanisms were not carried forward. Article, history, and suggest routes permanently redirect to the single current Cladosporium record.

revisedAssets.reason: Fine hair-like projections could read as pili or flagella and conflicted with the nonmotile framing.
revisedAssets.outcome: Targeted edit removed every appendage-like hair while preserving segmented branching rods and clubbed ends.

revisedAssets.reason: The upper-right cell carried a lophotrichous-looking polar tuft rather than the restrained single-polar form selected for the canonical genus treatment.
revisedAssets.outcome: Targeted edit removed the extra strands and retained exactly one fine polar flagellum on that cell without changing the other rods. Control-tower visual review accepted v2, and only v2 was promoted.

revisedAssets.reason: The first draft's seven bodies were visually clean but read as generic uniform curved bacilli and did not sufficiently communicate the documented normal curved-rod-or-bifid morphology.
revisedAssets.outcome: One authorized targeted replacement preserves seven bodies as five singles plus one two-cell pair while adding visible tapered poles, mild clubbing, and one restrained true bifid Y-ended body. Control-tower original-resolution review accepted v2, and only v2 was promoted.

revisedAssets.reason: The five complete bodies were aligned in near-parallel rows with repeated sine-wave geometry, producing an overly uniform decorative plate rather than five independent flexible forms.
revisedAssets.outcome: One targeted revision produced five separated bodies at distinct positions, lengths, axes, and amplitudes with broad irregular waves. Control human original-resolution review accepted v2, and only v2 was promoted.

revisedAssets.reason: Human original-resolution audit found fourteen bodies in ten groupings, not the prompt-requested twelve bodies in eight groupings.
revisedAssets.outcome: Revision 2 remained count-inconsistent and was not promoted; the review chain continued to revision 3.

revisedAssets.reason: Human original-resolution audit found nine bodies in seven groupings, not the prompt-requested ten bodies in seven groupings.
revisedAssets.outcome: Revision 3 reconciled exactly to eight bodies in six groupings, four singles plus two touching pairs. Control human original-resolution review accepted v3, and only v3 was promoted.

revisedAssets.reason: The lower-right three-rod grouping was enclosed by a shared translucent outer boundary that could read as an invented capsule, sheath, microcolony envelope, biofilm, or enclosing membrane and conflicted with the selected diversity-plate constraint.
revisedAssets.outcome: One targeted revision preserved nine bodies in five groupings while removing the shared outer boundary completely. Root original-resolution review accepted v2, and only v2 was promoted.

revisedAssets.reason: Control root found the otherwise clean nine-rod vegetative plate too generic for the Clostridioides difficile species page because it contained no visible endospores.
revisedAssets.outcome: Exactly one authorized revision produced ten rods in eight groupings, with two single rods each containing one restrained oval subterminal internal spore. Control root accepted v2 only; v1 was never used as a master or derivative.
